title: Comets, asteroids and meteors
examples: What is the difference between a comet and an asteroid?
If something burns up in the air, is it a meteor or a meteoroid?
Can we find meteorites on Earth?

explain.say: Today we learn about space rocks like comets and asteroids. These objects travel through space around the sun.
Asteroids are mostly made of rock and metal. They usually orbit in a belt between Mars and Jupiter.
Comets are very different because they have ice mixed with dust. This ice makes them look very bright.
A meteoroid is a small piece of rock or metal in space. It is just floating out there by itself.
When a meteoroid enters Earth's air, it burns up. We call that bright streak a meteor.
If a meteoroid survives and hits the ground, we call that solid piece a meteorite. It is a space rock on Earth.

faq.q: What is the difference between a meteoroid and a meteor?
faq.a: A meteoroid is the object floating in space. A meteor is the streak of light when it enters the atmosphere.
asks: Is a shooting star a meteoroid?
What is the light show in space?

faq.q: Are comets always made of ice?
faq.a: Comets have a mix of ice and dust. The ice is what makes them visible when they get close to the sun.

faq.q: How do we know if a rock is a meteorite?
faq.a: Scientists study its composition to see if it matches space rocks. Finding one on Earth is proof.
asks: What makes a rock a meteorite?

faq.q: Do asteroids and comets ever crash into each other?
faq.a: They are usually in different orbits, but collisions can happen over very long periods of time.
asks: Can space objects bump into each other?

faq.q: Is a shooting star always dangerous?
faq.a: No, the bright streak is usually just the rock burning up harmlessly in the air. It is not dangerous to us.
asks: What is a safe shooting star?

facts: Asteroids are primarily made of rock and metal.
Comets have a visible tail made of gas and dust.
A meteoroid is a space rock; a meteor is the streak of light.
A meteorite is a space rock that has reached Earth's surface.

quiz.say: Which object is mostly made of rock and metal and orbits in a belt?
quiz.why: Asteroids are known for being rocky bodies orbiting in a specific belt.

wrong.1: Comets are defined by their icy composition, not just rock.
wrong.2: Meteors are streaks of light, not the object itself.
wrong.3: Meteorites are only the pieces that hit the ground.

quiz.say: What is the name for a space rock burning up in the atmosphere?
quiz.why: The burning streak of light caused by atmospheric friction is called a meteor.

wrong.0: A comet is a different type of solar system body.
wrong.2: This is the object before it enters the air.
wrong.3: This only describes the object after it lands.

quiz.say: If a space rock hits Earth and you can pick it up, what is it called?
quiz.why: The term meteorite specifically means the object that has reached the Earth's surface.

wrong.0: This describes the light trail, not the solid object.
wrong.1: Asteroids orbit the sun, but they do not necessarily hit Earth.
wrong.3: This is the object still floating far out in space.
